extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners (patent owners, attorneys/agents, and third‑party requesters) handling inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules from the MPEP (Chapter 2600) governing optional inter partes reexamination of patents (statutory standards for institution, filing content/fees, processing, prosecution constraints, certificate issuance, and public access). Mostly addresses inter partes reexaminations filed prior to the AIA cutoff dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question (SNQ) of Patentability standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 312(a) (pre‑AIA SNQ standard), the Director determines whether a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim of the patent is raised by the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was the standard applicable for inter partes reexamination requests filed prior to September 16, 2011. If SNQ is present, reexamination will be ordered; if ordered under SNQ, the SNQ standard continues to apply throughout that reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable likelihood that requester will prevail standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Between Sept 16, 2011 and Sept 15, 2012, requests had to show that the information presented demonstrates a reasonable likelihood that the requester will prevail with respect to at least one challenged claim (per revised 35 U.S.C. 312 standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests filed on or after Sept 16, 2011 but before Sept 16, 2012 are judged by the 'reasonable likelihood' standard and, if ordered, that standard applies throughout the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: No inter partes reexamination requests accepted after Sept 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: As of Sept 16, 2012 the Office no longer entertains requests for inter partes reexamination and will not accord a filing date to such requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions to institute inter partes review (IPR) under the AIA are the post‑AIA mechanism; guidance for the former practice remains in the MPEP for reexaminations filed prior to the cutoff dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art considered is limited to patents and printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art during inter partes reexamination is limited to prior patents or printed publications applied under the appropriate parts of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other categories of information (e.g., certain testimonial evidence) are not a basis for rejection in reexamination; see MPEP §2202–2206 for details on making citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on request time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision on whether to grant a request for inter partes reexamination must be made not later than three months from its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the statutory standard is met, reexamination will be ordered and the remainder of proceedings must proceed with 'special dispatch' within the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reexamination cannot enlarge patent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of the patent claims cannot be enlarged by amendment during inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments may confirm, cancel, or incorporate new/amended claims but cannot broaden claim scope beyond original claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party requester participation and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party requester may participate throughout an inter partes reexamination proceeding and (post‑2002 expansion) has appeal rights including appeal to the Federal Circuit for requests filed prior to AIA changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third party requester may file comments, and is served certain communications. The reexamination procedure provides for a right of appeal notice rather than a final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access & official electronic file
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination and patent files are open to the public; the reexamination file is scanned to provide an electronic copy which is the official file of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All public access to and copying of reexamination proceedings is from the electronic copy; certain citation entries are delayed until after conclusion as set forth in 37 CFR 1.902.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing rules for prior art citations filed during pending reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a prior art citation satisfying 37 CFR 1.501 is submitted when an inter partes reexamination is pending, its treatment depends on who filed it and when:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A) Patent owner citations generally considered if timely before certificate issuance. B) Third‑party requester citations considered if submitted as part of required comments (37 CFR 1.947/1.951(b)) or in a proper request under 1.915/1.510. C) Other citations are retained until the reexamination concludes and only then placed in the patent file (per 37 CFR 1.902).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form of request for inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must contain certain elements specified in 37 CFR 1.915(b) and be accompanied by the required fee under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests submitted by an attorney/agent identifying another party must include power of attorney or show representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 (see 1.915(c)). Processing will not be delayed for absence of the power of attorney, but authority may later be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative of requester must be authorized
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney or agent acting for a requester must either have a power of attorney from the requester or act in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34; attorneys acting under a power of attorney must be registered patent practitioners (37 CFR 1.32(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authority questions arise, proof may be required. Correspondence is addressed to the requester’s representative unless instructed otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate of service is required for certain filings in inter partes reexamination (section headings indicate certificate of service as required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2620 for specifics; parties must ensure proper service and certificate entries as part of filing compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address and signature rules for patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: All Office communications are directed to the correspondence address in the patent file; amendments and papers filed on behalf of the patent owner must be signed by the patent owner (or all owners) or by authorized registered attorney/agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner wants a different attorney to receive correspondence a new power of attorney must be filed. Double correspondence (owner and owner’s attorney) is generally not undertaken by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of attorney/agent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To withdraw, practitioner must certify under 37 CFR 11.116 that they have (1) given reasonable notice to client prior to response period expiration, (2) delivered client papers/property, and (3) notified client of any responses due and time frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office no longer requires at least 30 days remaining; 'reasonable notice' should allow the client time to seek new counsel before response deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized papers and filing restrictions before first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers directed to the merits (other than prescribed categories) shall not be filed prior to the initial Office action on the merits; unauthorized papers will not be considered and may be returned (37 CFR 1.939).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted filings before initial action include: (A) citations of patents/printed publications under 37 CFR 1.501 & 1.933, (B) another complete request under 37 CFR 1.510, and (C) notifications per MPEP §2686; other merit papers filed prematurely are returned or expunged and a record is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing, delivery, and fax rules for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Original inter partes reexamination requests may not be sent by fax; correspondence and filings should be addressed to the specified Mail Stop and customer service locations; subsequent correspondence may be faxed to the Central Reexamination Unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing addresses and hand‑carry locations are provided. Use prominent Mail Stop info on first page in large font. Certificate of mailing and Priority Mail Express® procedures may be used for filing most papers (see MPEP §§512–513).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing (EFS-Web) allowed for requests and follow‑on papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Since July 9, 2007 the Office accepts inter partes reexamination requests and follow‑on papers via EFS‑Web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Legal Framework for EFS‑Web for specific procedures and allowed document types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and content of inter partes reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The inter partes reexamination certificate (titled 'INTER PARTES REEXAMINATION CERTIFICATE') will set forth the results of the proceeding, including canceling claims determined unpatentable, confirming patentable claims, incorporating amended/new claims determined patentable, listing changes in description, disclaimers, and identifying unamended claims held invalid or claims not reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New claims printed in italics; amended claims printed with italics and bracketing; certificate numbered with patent number + kind code suffix (C1, C2, etc.); certificate mailed to patent owner and copy to requester; bibliographic info similar to patent title page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights for amended or new claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Amended or new claims determined patentable and incorporated into the patent after inter partes reexamination have the same effect for intervening rights as specified in 35 U.S.C. 252 for reissued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects parties who made or prepared for use/import before issuance of the reexamination certificate; case law parallels noted (e.g., Fortel, Kaufman, Tennant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways a reexamination proceeding may be concluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination proceedings may be concluded by: (A) denial/vacation/termination (no certificate issued), (B) issuance of a reexamination certificate (37 CFR 1.997(b)), or (C) merger with a reissue proceeding where grant of a reissue patent serves as the certificate (37 CFR 1.997(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different procedural handling and status codes apply for each conclusion type (partial refunds, file processing, forwarding to Central Reexamination Unit, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination review and panel review before issuing Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: After examiner action and clerical processing, the case is forwarded to CRU SPRS or TC QAS for procedural and completeness review; a panel review is also made prior to issuing Office actions (MPEP §2671.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU/TC review checks compliance with statute/regulations, ensures issues/arguments from parties are developed and addressed, and ensures forms/references are present and complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interviews on merits in inter partes reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination proceedings do not permit interviews on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP specifically states 'No Interviews on Merits' as a procedural limitation; communications should follow prescribed filings and comment processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of statements under 35 U.S.C. 301(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions under 35 U.S.C. 301(a)(2) (statements of the patent owner filed in other proceedings) are not proper for an ongoing inter partes reexamination, as there is no statutory provision applying 301(a)(2) submissions to inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such statements should not be submitted in inter partes reexamination proceedings; see related MPEP sections for proper citation handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed USPTO forms and special documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific USPTO forms must be used in inter partes reexamination processing (PTOL‑2064, PTOL‑2065, PTOL‑2066, PTOL‑2068, PTOL‑476, PTOL‑2069, PTOL‑2070, PTOL‑2071, PTOL‑2072, PTOL‑2073, PTOL‑2291, PTOL‑1516, PTOL‑1517 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms include Office Action in Inter Partes Reexamination, Action Closing Prosecution, Right of Appeal Notice, Notice of Intent to Issue Certificate, Reexamination Reasons for Patentability/Confirmation, Notice of Defective Paper, transmittals to third party requester, examiner's answer, checklists, and others; using correct forms is required for proper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of amended/new claim text and presentation in certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: In the reexamination certificate new claims are printed entirely in italics; amended claims are printed with italics and bracketing indicating the amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate explicitly identifies which claims are confirmed, canceled, disclaimed, or not examined; it also references any prior court decisions affecting claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of improper earlier‑filed papers and expungement
rubrics_metrics.description: If improper papers are entered prior to discovery of impropriety, they will be expunged from the record and a copy of the notification of returned papers/expungement will be made of record in the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized filings (e.g., replies not permitted by regulation) will be returned and recorded; parties should file only papers provided for by reexamination regulations or seek petitions to accept/waive the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for requesting reexamination and for adding claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for inter partes reexamination must be accompanied by the fee required (37 CFR 1.20(c)(2)); fees are required for adding claims in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific fee amounts and fee processing procedures are set out in the regulations and MPEP; see the relevant MPEP sections for payment, partial refunds, and fee codes.
